cards.anchor: Complete exactly the K2/K5/K7 checked-status corrections, leave five others unchecked, make no incorrect-key write, preserve read-only scores, and load the latest snapshot within ten simulated minutes.
cards.burden: Six sequential selection/commit actions plus one final refresh cost seven minutes. Record each actual written key; never repair a miswrite and count the run successful. No external connector or macro is required.
cards.construction: Start on loaded S0. Inspect/select K2 during 0-1 and commit during 1-2; select K5 during 2-3 and commit during 3-4; select K7 during 4-5 and commit during 5-6. Keep S0 loaded across all writes, then refresh during 6-7 to load S2. Compare the complete write log and final status map by immutable key.
cards.defeat: Reject if any actual write targets another key, any target or nontarget status is wrong, S2 is absent at submission, scores were edited, or completion exceeds ten minutes. A wrong write remains a defeat even if repaired.
cards.mutation: Remove every intermediate refresh while retaining the original row-bound editor; move freshness fulfillment after the last commit. Selection uses explicit keys, including the equal-score K5/K7 boundary.
cards.prediction_candidate: Hypothesis: stable loaded S0 keeps selections at rows 2, 5 and 7 through their commits, giving exactly K2/K5/K7 writes. Key-persistent statuses survive the final S2 refresh; total time is seven minutes and incorrect-key writes are zero.
cards.prediction_rival: The strict necessity account predicts this replay cannot attain the complete outcome because no commit has its asserted immediate-refresh prerequisite. A verified seven-minute success would falsify that claim within this model.
cards.probe: Execute the declared seven-minute replay from all-unchecked S0; log action times, loaded snapshots, retained rows, intended keys, every written key and final statuses. Judge final freshness and write history jointly. The supplied trace is only the separate select-refresh-commit miswrite.
cards.rival: Immediate refresh before every commit is necessary for reliable, latest-compliant correction.
unknowns: This completion replay is unexecuted; prospective success follows stipulated rules only.
Real editor binding, detection costs and reliability are unknown.
Concurrent status changes, deletion and load failures are outside the model.

cards.anchor: Preserve the same exact-target, zero-miswrite outcome and final S2 freshness within ten minutes while retaining three scheduled refreshes.
cards.burden: Six selection/commit actions plus three refreshes cost nine minutes absent executed return refreshes. Any additional return refresh consumes the one remaining minute; q+h greater than four makes completion infeasible. Stop on the first incorrect-key write.
cards.construction: With row binding, refresh during 0-1, select K2 during 1-2, commit during 2-3; refresh during 3-4, select K5 during 4-5, commit during 5-6; refresh during 6-7, select K7 during 7-8, commit during 8-9. A refresh may precede selection but never intervene between selection and its commit. Retain mismatch-triggered requests and log requests separately from executed refreshes.
cards.defeat: The construction fails with any wrong-key write, incorrect final status, score edit, missing final S2 or budget overrun. Comparable initial errors with frozen order or immutable-key binding would weaken its reorder explanation. Diagnostic controls do not establish completion freshness.
cards.mutation: Hold the three-refresh dose fixed and relocate refreshes before selection. Treat the selection-to-commit interval as an uninterrupted pair; retain original row binding and the mismatch-request rule.
cards.prediction_candidate: Hypothesis: the preselection arm writes K2/K5/K7 correctly in nine minutes with S2 loaded. At the same three-refresh dose and commit times, the postselection arm first writes K5 when K2 was intended. Frozen-order and key-bound controls predict no initial identity error.
cards.prediction_rival: A dose-only explanation predicts comparable identity failures at three refreshes regardless of their placement. Correct preselection writes alongside the postselection miswrite would defeat that explanation; a five-refresh schedule still exceeds ten minutes even with correct binding.
cards.probe: Replay preselection and postselection arms from identical S0 with three refreshes, target demand, tie ordering and commit slots 2-3/5-6/8-9 fixed. Postselection begins select 0-1, refresh 1-2, commit 2-3. Cross changing/frozen snapshots with row/key binding using R5. Stop failing arms on any miswrite; record request counts separately. Full-outcome scoring applies only to latest-compliant completion arms.
cards.rival: Refresh frequency itself causes identity errors; placement relative to selection has no separating effect.
unknowns: The nine-minute completion and control replays remain unexecuted.
O5 supplies one miswrite; dose dependence and repeated return-refresh errors are unobserved.
Timing shifts change which snapshot loads; the crossed controls test the identity mechanism, not real human usability.
Real binding, interruptions and concurrent failures remain outside available evidence.
